page: Microsoft Azure D64plds_v7 is an ARM64-based virtual machine deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V, featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. Bundled hardware includes 3,780 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The 64-bit ARM architecture delivers high-density compute capacity suited for multithreaded applications compiled for ARM. The 2.0 GB per core ratio represents a compute-focused profile, trading deep memory capacity for increased CPU concurrency. The inclusion of 3,780 GB of fast NVMe local storage provides low-latency ephemeral disk capacity, avoiding total reliance on networked storage for intense read and write activity.

Given its combination of 64 dedicated ARM vCPUs, moderate memory density, and substantial local NVMe storage, the D64plds_v7 fits parallel compute tasks requiring rapid local scratch space. Relevant workloads include large-scale software compilation, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, batch data transformations, video transcode queues, and distributed web serving clusters.
